title: B. ATOMIC STRUCTURE — Q31–60 (part 1)
source: Chemistry MCQ Test OPTIMIZED — B. ATOMIC STRUCTURE — Q31–60, pages 2-2 [Chemistry_MCQ_Test_OPTIMIZED.md]
textbookText: 31. Rutherford's gold foil (alpha-particle scattering) experiment led to the conclusion that: A) The atom has a small, dense, positively charged nucleus with most of the atom being empty space B) Electrons are embedded in a uniform sphere of positive charge (plum pudding model) C) The atom is indivisible and has no internal structure D) All the mass of the atom is uniformly spread throughout its volume

32. In Rutherford's experiment, the fact that most alpha particles passed straight through the gold foil indicated: A) Most of the atom's volume is empty space B) The nucleus occupies most of the atom's volume C) Atoms have no positive charge at all D) Gold atoms are much smaller than alpha particles

33. The small fraction of alpha particles that bounced back at large angles in Rutherford's experiment indicated: A) A concentrated, massive, positively charged nucleus repelling the positively charged alpha particles B) Electrons colliding with alpha particles C) The foil being too thick for particles to pass through D) Alpha particles being negatively charged

34. A major limitation of Rutherford's atomic model was that it: A) Could not explain why orbiting electrons don't spiral into the nucleus while losing energy (violating classical electromagnetic theory) B) Could not explain the existence of the nucleus at all C) Predicted atoms have no electrons D) Correctly explained atomic spectra, which was later disproved

35. According to classical electromagnetic theory, an accelerating (orbiting) electron should: A) Continuously radiate energy and spiral into the nucleus, making atoms unstable — contradicted by observed atomic stability B) Remain in a fixed, stable orbit forever without energy loss C) Never radiate any energy under any circumstances D) Immediately escape the atom entirely

36. Bohr's first postulate states that: A) Electrons revolve around the nucleus only in certain fixed, allowed circular orbits called stationary states, without radiating energy B) Electrons can occupy any arbitrary orbit and radiate energy continuously C) The nucleus revolves around the electron D) All orbits have exactly the same energy

37. Bohr's postulate about angular momentum states that the angular momentum of an electron in an orbit is quantized as: A) mvr = nh/2π, where n is a positive integer (principal quantum number) B) mvr = h × n² C) mvr = nh² (no division by 2π) D) mvr is always zero

38. According to Bohr's theory, an electron emits radiation (a photon) when it: A) Jumps from a higher energy orbit to a lower energy orbit B) Remains in the same orbit indefinitely C) Jumps from a lower to a higher energy orbit, releasing energy D) Is completely removed from the atom (ionization) only
39. The energy of a photon emitted during an electronic transition is given by: A) E = hν = E_higher − E_lower B) E = hν = E_lower − E_higher (positive value implied) C) E = h/ν D) E = mc² only

40. The Lyman series in the hydrogen spectrum corresponds to electronic transitions ending at: A) n = 1 (ground state), emitting in the ultraviolet region B) n = 2, emitting in the visible region C) n = 3, emitting in the infrared region D) n = infinity
41. The Balmer series of the hydrogen spectrum, which includes visible lines, corresponds to transitions ending at: A) n = 2 B) n = 1 C) n = 3 D) n = 4
42. Which series of the hydrogen spectrum lies in the infrared region, ending at n = 3? A) Paschen series B) Lyman series C) Balmer series D) Brackett series
43. The Rydberg formula for the hydrogen spectrum is: A) 1/λ = R(1/n₁² − 1/n₂²), where R is the Rydberg constant B) 1/λ = R(n₁² − n₂²) C) λ = R(1/n₁ − 1/n₂) D) 1/λ = R × n₁ × n₂

44. A major defect of Bohr's theory is that it: A) Could not explain the spectra of multi-electron atoms (only worked well for hydrogen-like species) B) Could not explain the hydrogen spectrum at all C) Failed to introduce the concept of quantized orbits D) Predicted electrons have no energy levels

45. Bohr's theory also failed to explain: A) The fine structure (splitting) of spectral lines observed under high resolution B) The existence of the hydrogen spectrum's main lines C) The stability of the ground state of hydrogen D) The quantization of angular momentum

46. Bohr's theory could not account for which experimentally observed effect on atomic spectra in a magnetic field? A) The Zeeman effect (splitting of spectral lines in a magnetic field) B) The photoelectric effect C) The Compton effect D) Radioactive decay

47. Bohr's model also could not explain which effect observed when atoms are placed in an electric field? A) The Stark effect (splitting of spectral lines in an electric field) B) The Doppler effect C) The greenhouse effect D) The tunnel effect
